clue.text: A crowd of journalists

definitions.meaning: a crush or throng of people pushing together
reporters and newspapers collectively, as in freedom of the newspapers' trade

explanation.surface: A pack of reporters jostling for a story.
explanation.definitionFit: A throng is a press of people, and the newspaper trade and its reporters are collectively the press.

clue.text: Grey worried — major flap about commendatory speech

indicators.note: the alarm goes around the shuffled colour, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: a major flap is a panic, a state of great alarm

indicators.note: being troubled or fretful suggests these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A grey-faced official is in a fluster while delivering words of praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' turns GREY into EGYR, and 'about' sets PANIC around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A panegyric is a formal public eulogy, a speech full of praise.

clue.text: How thus to praise, one made mighty by God ?

definitions.text: How thus to praise, one made mighty by God ?

parts.words: How thus to praise, one made mighty by God ?
parts.note: asks for the verb used for lauding someone the Psalms say God has exalted and made mighty

explanation.surface: A question about the proper way to honour a hero raised up by heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: Psalm 89 speaks of one God has 'exalted' and laid help upon as mighty; the verb for lifting such a person up in praise is the one wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud or glorify someone highly is to sing their praises in elevated terms.

clue.text: Money that keeps the revs going

definitions.text: Money that keeps the revs going

parts.words: Money that keeps the revs going
parts.note: revs looks like engine revolutions, but here it is short for Reverends, clergy kept alive by regular salaries

explanation.surface: Fuel money that keeps an engine turning over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revs' suggests an engine; it is the abbreviation of Reverends, and clergy are paid fixed salaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Clergy are traditionally paid a fixed salary called by this name.

clue.text: We get our teeth into the subject of inflation

definitions.text: We get our teeth into the subject of inflation

parts.words: We get our teeth into the subject of inflation
parts.note: inflation sounds economic, but it is the blowing of a chewy confection into a balloon

explanation.surface: Economists tackling the topic of rising prices with vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inflation' points to economics; the thing chewed and blown up is a sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A chewy confection that can be blown into balloons, and so is literally inflated.

clue.text: 'Tell 'me where is, fancy — (Mer of Venice)

parts.note: a quotation to complete, the song sung while Bassanio chooses a casket in Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blank line from a Shakespeare song.
explanation.walkthrough: The song in The Merchant of Venice runs 'Tell me where is fancy bred, Or in the heart or in the head?'
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word of the lyric is a past participle meaning born or raised.

clue.text: As profound as Thisbe played without Pyramus

parts.note: in A Midsummer Night's Dream, Pyramus is played by Nick Bottom the weaver
without means lacking, which is the suffix less

explanation.surface: A remark on how deep an amateur performance of Thisbe becomes when her lover is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: In the mechanicals' play Bottom acts Pyramus, so a Thisbe played without Pyramus is played without Bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Something profound in the sense of immeasurably deep has no floor to reach.

clue.text: Bee sound for instance?

parts.note: not a buzz: the letter B, a consonant made with the lips

explanation.surface: A question about the noise an insect makes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bee' is the letter B, made by closing the lips, as are P and M.
explanation.definitionFit: A consonant articulated with the lips, as B, P and M are, is a lip sound.

clue.text: Soap, water-what next.?

parts.note: soap and water give cleanliness, and the proverb says cleanliness is next to a holy virtue

explanation.surface: Someone asking what comes after the washing things.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'Cleanliness is next to godliness': soap and water stand for cleanliness, so what is next is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Piety or holiness, which the old saying ranks just after being clean.

clue.text: Touchy transmuter

parts.note: touchy means not irritable but turning things to gold by touch, as the Phrygian king of myth did

explanation.surface: A thin-skinned alchemist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touchy' suggests easily offended; the king of legend changed whatever he touched into gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical king whose touch turned everything, even food, to gold.

clue.text: As food, a nut is without unusual merit and point

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so these letters are set in an odd order

parts.note: N is north, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A dietary note that a nut lacks any remarkable merit or purpose as food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges MERIT with N into RIMENT, which follows NUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nourishment, anything that feeds a living thing.

clue.text: Awaited the time for quitting the port of Devon

indicators.note: for quitting means that word leaves the place name

parts.note: Bideford is a port in north Devon, a county in south-west England
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone waiting for the moment to leave a Devon harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quitting' takes FOR out of BIDEFORD, a port in Devon (a south-west English county).
explanation.definitionFit: To bide one's time is to wait patiently for the right moment.

clue.text: Are printer's devils such slaves ?

parts.note: a printer's devil is an errand boy in a print shop, where type proofs are taken on a tray of the same name as an oared ship

explanation.surface: A question about whether print-shop apprentices are overworked.
explanation.walkthrough: Slaves chained to oars in a ship were this kind of slave; a printer works with proofs on a tray of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Both an oared ship rowed by slaves and the printer's tray holding set type.

clue.text: He lacked a fourth at bridge

definitions.text: He lacked a fourth at bridge

parts.words: He lacked a fourth at bridge
parts.note: not the card game: the Roman who held a bridge over the Tiber against an army with just two comrades

explanation.surface: A card player unable to make up a table.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge needs four players; the Roman hero defended the Sublician bridge as one of three, so he was a fourth short.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman hero Cocles, who in legend kept the bridge against Lars Porsena.

clue.text: Put in other words, a quiet share, adjustment under nominal value

indicators.note: in a down clue the later pieces sit beneath the first one

parts.note: par is the face or nominal value of a share
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: an adjustment alters the arrangement, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A stock-market report of a small share price change below face value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjustment' turns SHARE into HRASE; 'under' places A, P and that below PAR in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To restate something in different language is to reword it.

clue.text: Designed for a conference of 150 knights?

definitions.text: Designed for a conference of 150 knights?

parts.words: Designed for a conference of 150 knights?
parts.note: the furniture at Camelot, said in some tellings to seat 150 knights so none sat at its head

explanation.surface: A question about furniture built for a huge medieval meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Malory and other sources give King Arthur's famous table seats for 150 knights; the phrase also means a conference of equals.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur's table, and by extension a discussion among equals with no head.

clue.text: They 'may give, a lift to potential down-and-outs

definitions.text: They 'may give, a lift to potential down-and-outs

parts.words: They 'may give, a lift to potential down-and-outs
parts.note: down-and-outs here are boxers about to be knocked down, and the lift is an upward punch

explanation.surface: Charity workers helping people who are on the verge of destitution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down-and-outs' suggests the destitute; a boxer knocked down and counted out is down and out, and upward punches lift the chin.
explanation.definitionFit: Upward punches to the chin in boxing.

clue.text: Swarms of sempstresses

parts.note: swarms suggests insects, but sewing groups gathered to work together are named after the hive

explanation.surface: Crowds of seamstresses.
explanation.walkthrough: A gathering of women sewing together is a sewing bee, so swarms of them are this word.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects in swarms, and also social gatherings for communal work such as sewing.

clue.text: Odd girl that's guiding certain poor shepherds.

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the following letters are put in a strange order

explanation.surface: An eccentric girl leading a group of impoverished shepherds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' rearranges GIRL THATS. The carol The First Nowell tells of the angel coming 'to certain poor shepherds', and a star guided them.
explanation.definitionFit: The light of the star of Bethlehem led the shepherds in the carol.

clue.text: Boy is getting cocktails

parts.note: Martin is a boy's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young man drinking cocktails.
explanation.definitionFit: Gin-and-vermouth cocktails.

clue.text: A head on one's shoulders

parts.note: a head here is a headland, and the garment rests on the shoulders

explanation.surface: A remark about being sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is a headland; the same word names a cloak worn over the shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a headland jutting into the sea and a sleeveless cloak over the shoulders.

clue.text: God takes Henry to the main prison

parts.note: Mars is the Roman god of war
Hal is a familiar form of Henry, as Shakespeare's Prince Hal
the main is a poetic term for the open sea

explanation.surface: A deity escorting a king to the chief jail.
explanation.walkthrough: The Marshalsea was a notorious London debtors' prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic Southwark jail for debtors, featured in Dickens.

clue.text: Sundry 'submarine, types

definitions.meaning: an old adjective meaning various or several
people who work under the sea

explanation.surface: A mixed bag of underwater people.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adjective for several or various, and people who plunge underwater.

clue.text: Cliff-hanging way to ruin the rich once

indicators.note: ruining something wrecks its form, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A precarious mountain road that could bankrupt wealthy people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ruin' rearranges RICH ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A road cut into a cliff face along a coast.

clue.text: Raised to power, is the editor as green as the reporter ?.

parts.note: a cub reporter is a novice, green at the job

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor suspected of being as inexperienced as his junior staff.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'cub reporter' is a beginner; CUB then ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Multiplied by itself to the third power in mathematics.

clue.text: No tonic is prescribed for such music makers

definitions.text: No tonic is prescribed for such music makers

parts.words: No tonic is prescribed for such music makers
parts.note: tonic sounds medical, but it is the home note of a key, which some modern composers avoid

explanation.surface: A doctor refusing to give musicians a pick-me-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tonic' suggests medicine; in music it is the keynote, and music written without a key has none.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing music written without a key or tonal centre.

clue.text: Simple 'single-hearted Welsh boy is upset

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters read bottom to top
hearted means the number sits at the centre of the name

parts.note: Evan is a Welsh boy's name
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A guileless Welsh lad with a kind heart is distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearted' puts I inside EVAN to give EVIAN, and 'is upset' turns that backwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Artless, innocent and unworldly.

clue.text: Time' of prosperity for a sail-stretcher

definitions.meaning: a period of rapid economic growth
a spar that extends the foot of a sail

explanation.surface: Good times for a sailmaker.
explanation.definitionFit: An economic upswing, and the spar along the bottom edge of a fore-and-aft sail.

clue.text: He showed more fight than Miss Muffet

definitions.text: He showed more fight than Miss Muffet

parts.words: He showed more fight than Miss Muffet
parts.note: the nursery-rhyme girl fled from a spider, whereas the Scottish king was inspired by one to keep fighting

explanation.surface: A man braver than the nursery-rhyme girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Miss Muffet ran from a spider; Robert the Bruce, king of Scots, watched a spider persist and took heart to fight on.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert the Bruce, the Scottish king of the spider legend.

clue.text: By this (not in a gin cocktail) I may get oiled

definitions.text: By this (not in a gin cocktail) I may get oiled

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so these letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: A drinker contemplating getting oiled without gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' mixes NOT IN A GIN. 'Oiled' looks like drunk, but anointing is literally applying oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Smearing with oil, as in a religious ceremony.

clue.text: Think about one. Tess, unhappily in bad odour

indicators.note: the verb goes around the other pieces, so it holds them inside

parts.note: to deem is to think or judge
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: unhappily signals the name is put into a disordered state

explanation.surface: A reflection on Tess of the d'Urbervilles, sadly out of favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhappily' turns TESS into SEST; 'about' wraps DEEM round I and SEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in bad odour means being out of favour, the state of low regard.

clue.text: Delightful, the set of rooms sounds

indicators.note: sounds says the word for the rooms is heard, not seen

parts.note: a suite is a set of connected rooms, as in a hotel

explanation.surface: Praise for a charming hotel apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Charming or pleasing.
